items.new_text: Place a conversation without a creation timestamp last: it is not the oldest, but one whose start is unknown. Match Desk's `null` ordering.
Apply the quick filter in `where` for both open and closed populations
so cards and table describe the same selection.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.

Monitoring queries only combine database events with calculations from `@pipe/core`; metrics shown on screen come from `2026-09-05-metricas-atendimento.md`. Group by queue, agent and label in memory over the day's rows for now. Move to PostgreSQL `group by` or `metrica_diaria` when a tenant reaches several thousand conversations per day.
Open pause exceeding its reason's suggested duration.
Touch only relevant partitions; an open-conversation event is not historical.
Parameterize the time-zone expression and refer to it by position
so PostgreSQL sees identical `SELECT`, `GROUP BY` and `ORDER BY` expressions.
Closed-conversation count for the period, used by the history header.
Queue seconds stop on assignment, or continue while unassigned.
The agent owes the next response: the customer spoke last or nobody has answered yet.

Report the population behind the maximum. A maximum without population has the same problem as an average without denominator (metrics spec §2): 40 minutes among two conversations calls for a different response than among 200.
Model-reported mean confidence from 0 to 1, for AI evaluations only.
Highest possible score of the most-used form in the period, giving the scale for the mean.

Average scores with explicit population. Exclude draft evaluations and those without a score; return their excluded count so the screen can show a denominator that does not improve invisibly as the process worsens.
Group the already loaded list in memory, not with `GROUP BY`, using the SAME exclusion rule as the overall average so table and card agree.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
Points on the final-score scale, allowing the screen to say how many points were lost here.

AI quality review displays the evaluation result. `packages/ai` scores each criterion deterministically (`avaliacao/nota.ts`), cites supporting messages and stores `avaliacao` plus `resposta_avaliacao`; supervisors previously had no screen for paid model calls. Display the mean's population and exclusions: drafts and unscored evaluations can otherwise inflate it. Weight by evaluation volume (§5): sum scores divided by evaluation count, never average agent averages. This module accepts data and returns data without Next (README, 'Quem fala com o banco'). Query SERIALly inside `consultar`: `Promise.all` can clear `pipe.tenant_id` and silently disable RLS tenant filtering.
Resolve the AI-cited excerpt to its message text.
Sum of points before a fatal criterion zeroes the score, showing the magnitude of the loss.
Names of failed fatal criteria; empty if none zeroed the score.
Conversation-classification summary, when AI also classified it.
The URL path ID is untrusted. Without validation, `/monitoria/abc` reaches PostgreSQL as `abc::uuid` and the screen returns 500; `null` here becomes the correct 404 upstream.
Return the whole form, including unanswered criteria: an unanswered criterion means incomplete evaluation and the detail screen must show that gap.
Fetch cited messages in one query. `mensagem` is partitioned with uniqueness on `(id, criada_em)`, so `evidencia_mensagem_id` has no foreign key; joining by ID is enough for display.
States with a final usable score; drafts are not counted because nobody finalized them.
`null` while evaluation has no final score, so it is excluded from the mean.
Count zero-scored evaluations caused by a fatal criterion; the mean alone hides them.
Overall mean score alongside its population and exclusions.
Count AI and human evaluations separately; an AI score remains a suggestion until reviewed.

Read quality-review scores for the screen without recalculating: `packages/ai/src/avaliacao/nota.ts` already stored per-criterion points in `resposta_avaliacao` on the final-score scale. This layer identifies which fatal criterion failed; `avaliacao.nota` records zero but not its cause. `TETO_ESCALA` and `TETO_NOTA` match `packages/ai/src/avaliacao/tipos.ts` and are duplicated because `@pipe/ai` loads a model client and must not become a Management dependency; the test below detects divergence.
Fraction of a criterion met, from 0 to 1; `null` when inapplicable or unanswered.

A failed fatal criterion zeroes the whole evaluation. Match `calcularNota`: failure requires a known fraction LESS THAN 1. Unanswered and not-applicable fatal criteria do not fail; treating absence as failure would turn an incomplete form into a zero-scored agent.
Read this tenant's ACTIVE forbidden terms from cache or database on every `envio.ts` message. Cache avoids a database query per send for a rarely changing list.
Invalidate the cached list; without a tenant, clear all lists for tests.
Check text against the tenant's forbidden terms and throw when matched. Match source toast `forbiddenWords.title`/`forbiddenWords.text`: title 'Palavras proibidas' and matched terms in quotes.
Trim outer whitespace and collapse inner whitespace so equivalent phrases register as one term.
The database unique key uses `lower(termo)`, but registration also ignores accents: the filter treats 'açúcar' and 'acucar' as one term, so storing both would confuse the list.
Leave the type unannotated: the inferred literal satisfies `Record<string, unknown>` in `diferenca`.

Reuse the General Settings catalog permission. Forbidden terms are account-wide attendance configuration like identity and survey; Blip stores them in bot settings (`HasForbiddenWords`, `blip-gestao-regras-tecnicas.md`).
Match the source tokenizer regex (`app.js:77445`) exactly, including that hyphens do not split tokens: 'bem-vindo' stays one token.
Implement intended `StringUtils.normalizeText(texto, lower, diacritics, collapse)`: lowercase, remove accents and collapse whitespace.
Like source `checkForbiddenWords`, return matching registered terms in their stored spelling for the quoted refusal; empty means sending is allowed.
First pass checks phrases: `checkForbiddenPhrases` (`app.js:77427`) uses a plain substring

Forbidden terms block agent sends per `referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-desk-regras-tecnicas.md` §3.4. Source bucket `lime://<owner>/buckets/blip:desk:forbidden-words` is per bot owner; Pipe uses a tenant table (migration 0042). Filter only agent free text in Desk `sendTextMessage` via `envio.ts`, before delivery; bots and active-message templates bypass it. On match, block, list terms in quotes and leave input intact; Pipe returns `ErroPipe` 400 with matched terms in `detalhe`. Match source `checkForbiddenWords` (app.js:77434-77455): first phrase substrings over the whole text, returning only phrases if any match; otherwise split into `SEPARADORES` tokens and use `token.includes(termo)`. Normalize case, accents and whitespace. Source has a diacritics branch bug that loses lowercase; Pipe follows intended behavior, so `PALAVRA`, `palavra`, and `pálavra` match. Cache per tenant for five minutes (`CONFIGURATION_EXPIRATION_FORBIDDEN_WORDS_TIME`, 300000 ms) and invalidate on CRUD. Pipe fixes source defaults for `exactMatch` and `considerDiacritics` because no screen exposes them. Do not copy source fail-open: this server filter runs in the send transaction, whose database failure already aborts the send.

Compute setup-wizard steps from database facts. Chatwoot onboarding (`app/javascript/dashboard/routes/dashboard/onboarding/`, MIT) orders account data, channels (`InboxSetup.vue`, WhatsApp first), then team (`invite_team`). Pipe adds a staffed queue, contacts and a test conversation to reach first service. Chatwoot stores a click-advanced `onboarding_step` cursor; Pipe queries whether each required thing exists, so a visited screen alone cannot mark a step complete. Keep this module pure for `node --test`.
Connected channels marked for reauthorization, such as failed webhooks or a number pending at Meta.
Active users including the administrator.

Load the whole catalog with each requested agent's permission state. Run queries SERIALLY, never under `Promise.all`: parallel work on one connection can clear transaction `set_config('pipe.tenant_id')` and stop RLS filtering.
One row per person and permission granted by a ROLE; use `selectDistinct` because multiple roles often grant the same permission.

The agent Permissions page mirrors source `attendance.desk.team.permission` as a PAGE, not modal (`referencias-blip/fichas/FICHA-atendentes-filas-pausas.md` §§a.1/a.4). Keep source literal labels 'Permissões', 'Configure as permissões de …', 'Permissões disponíveis', 'Tipo de permissão', 'Status', and 'Salvar alterações', but populate rows from Pipe's enforced catalog (`packages/db/src/semente.ts`) rather than Blip's ten Desk capabilities (`canSendActiveMessage`, `canCallsVideo`, etc.). Migration 0046 adds per-person `usuario_permissao` override: effective = `COALESCE(override, union of roles)`. Delete an override when the choice matches the role again, avoiding stale copies of RBAC. For multi-agent selection (`single`, `couple`, `multiples`), show a permission on only when ALL have it and `parcial` when mixed; saving without touching a mixed row must not silently revoke anyone.

With one agent, `dosPapeis` and `override` describe that agent. With several, the screen needs only `ligada`/`parcial`; those two fields describe the first solely for the single-selection Status column.
Only permissions the screen CHANGED: code to enabled/disabled; leave all others as they are.
On 'Salvar alterações', write an override for each requested person and code, or DELETE it when the selected value already matches the role grant.
The choice matches the role again, so remove the exception.
Audit only actual changes; saving without edits is not an event.
Catalog permission 'Criar, editar e desativar usuário' governs changing others' permissions.

Expose only AGENT capabilities on this page. Blip lists ten Desk actions such as 'Transferir tickets' and 'Editar dados do contato'; including Pipe's whole catalog would let an agent receive API-key issuance or role-management powers through an override, bypassing roles. Conversation and contact capabilities belong here; the rest stay role-controlled.
Use literal source labels where the capability is equivalent.
Union of role grants before per-person exceptions.
`null` means no override; use the role grant.
Whether the permission is currently effective for ALL requested agents.
Some agents have it and others do not; possible only with multiple agents.
Reject duplicate, empty or out-of-tenant IDs; the screen sends its selected agents.

Survey scale, metrics spec §6. Blip has two incompatible models. Pipe supports both but requires ONE type-derived scale per survey and stores the scale on each response, so a CSAT 4 and NPS 4 cannot be summed together. Do not let the configuration form type an arbitrary scale such as 'CSAT de 0 a 10'. Keep this module pure because the `'use client'` configuration card imports it.
Expose spec §6 boundaries as text so the screen does not repeat numbers by hand.
Survey trigger: the database accepts free text, but the screen offers these three values.

Classify a score within its survey type's scale. Keep this separate from `satisfacao.ts`, which reads the class stored with historical responses; configuration previews what scores will mean before save, without reclassifying the past.
